column3: FortuneSheet's MIT licence text, read at build time by tsdown.config.ts and injected as a commented banner into the published client.excel.js chunk because FortuneSheet omits it from its npm payload.
Marketplace metadata: {"meta":{"title":"ui-sidebar-documentpreview"}} — the English title is the raw package id.
Chinese marketplace metadata: title 文档预览面板 plus a description the English dictionary lacks.

Manifest: name/version 0.2.1-rc.2, dsh.client.inject list of 8 sibling plugins, and the heavy parsers (exceljs, xlsx from the SheetJS CDN, pdfjs-dist, FortuneSheet) as devDependencies because they are bundled not imported.
Bilingual-pair hash record pinning each README heading's English and Chinese blocks; re-recorded by pnpm run verify-translation-pairing --write.

The package contract: the two-stage registration, the three loading modes, the HTML sandbox policy, the Excel and Office limits, navigation, and an unusually honest Known Limitations section (failed PDF chunk needs a page reload; scroll writes unthrottled).
Chinese translation of the same contract, read in full; it preserves the reasoning (e.g. the background/foreground cache slot reservation) rather than translating only the nouns.
Code renderer layout: the pane's own background instead of the chat card fill, and the code banner as the scrollport's sibling so the source scrollbar starts below it.

Renders the accumulated text as ONE CodeBlock with streaming={!content.eof}, so a partially downloaded file highlights as a growing single block and a comment spanning a page boundary keeps its colour.
Registers the code renderer at the builtin band over CODE_HIGHLIGHT_EXTENSIONS with loading text-pages and wrap true, plus its keyed body.
Four-key dictionary (title, copy, copied) whose key set is also the LocaleNamespaceMap declaration for sidebarCodePreview.

The text tab type: pattern dsh-resource://file/[\s\S]+ (a character-class repetition so literal . and .. segments survive), priority fallback, canOpen restricted to session-scoped addresses, and basenameOf that keeps a malformed percent escape raw.
The renderer contract: DocumentContent is text | bytes | a renderer HANDSHAKE carrying revision/loaded/failed/reload, plus the four slot declarations and the one-line documentTabInfoFactory adapter.

Observable registry of renderers: ranks ALL matches (extension band, then longest suffix, then registration order), rejects a binary suffix outside its own extensions, rejects duplicate ids, and publishes a stable snapshot.
Dependency membership for one preview: the first metadata frame is a baseline, only a later change invalidates, and a repeated identical failure is not a change.
The one suffix matcher shared by the registry and the unviewable list: returns the longest matching suffix LENGTH (for ranking) and treats \ and / alike.
Releases a renderer's retained view state on tab closure or plugin disposal, keyed by AbortSignal so repeated holds share one listener.
The known-binary-suffix list (video, audio, archives, office, binaries, fonts, images) with 'key' deliberately excluded so credential files keep the plain-text fallback.
Ambient declarations for the two build-time imports the Excel chunk uses: *.ts?raw for the worker source and @fortune-sheet/react/dist/index.css?inline for the scoped stylesheet.
Format dispatch: re-checks the byte limit on the worker side of the trust boundary, then routes to convertXlsx, convertXls or convertDelimited.
CSV/TSV parsing that keeps every value a literal string (dynamicTyping false plus the '@' number format) and FAILS the table on malformed quoting rather than dropping data.
The four locale-independent failure categories (invalid, tooLarge, timeout, encoding) — the closed set the UI can say something useful about.

The read-only spreadsheet surface: FortuneSheet with allowEdit false and forceCalculation false, the third-party CSS injected under @scope, a ResizeObserver dispatching a synthetic window resize, and a separate formula-result warning.
Spreadsheet layout and the :global overrides that hide FortuneSheet's editing handles and freeze drag handles, with color-scheme light so the third-party grid stays legible in a dark app.
Filename-to-parser selection kept outside the heavy chunk, so a .xlsm is rejected without downloading FortuneSheet, ExcelJS, SheetJS and PapaParse.
Registers the spreadsheet renderer for xlsx/xls/csv/tsv with only xlsx and xls declared binary — CSV and TSV keep the plain-text fallback — independently of the Office conversion service.
Defers the whole spreadsheet chunk until a workbook is opened, resolving the parser from the file suffix in the main bundle.
The spreadsheet dictionary, including the per-feature notice names and featureSeparator, plus the FortuneSheet 'language' key (zh/en) handed to the third-party grid.
The shared display model: the closed ordered EXCEL_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURES vocabulary, the three limits, initialSelection (A1 including an A1 merge) and formatCell (never evaluates a formula).

Runs the parser in a disposable Worker with a deadline, transferring a COPY of the retained bytes; the Worker message is validated as untrusted input (validPreview) and every exit path terminates the Worker, revokes the URL and clears the timer.
The 12-line Worker entry that owns the private response protocol {ok,value|code} — the whole trust boundary between the browser and four third-party parsers.

Legacy BIFF decoding: a magic-number check refuses renamed text/HTML files before SheetJS sees them, the 1904 epoch adds 1462 to date serials, and a real BIFF CellParsedFormula token array is read as a formula.

Builds an in-memory copy of the XLSX with DrawingML parts omitted (source bytes never modified), normalises the Strict-OOXML relationship URI, refuses package-root escapes, and REJECTS ambiguous ASCII case-equivalent ZIP entries.

XLSX to FortuneSheet conversion: the cell-area limit is enforced incrementally as the bounding rectangle grows, theme colours and OOXML tints are re-implemented, and cell.result (not cell.value) is used so a cached 0 or false survives.

The preview's async half: a per-tab monotonic generation counter is the stale-result guard, mode or renderer change aborts and resets, and a page of a NEWER file version past line 1 restarts the walk rather than mixing versions.
Maps each workspace-file code to one sentence and, separately, to the empty-state recourse (open | retry | none) — so a not-text file is handed elsewhere instead of being retried forever.

Builds the inert static HTML document: DOMPurify runs BEFORE the policy, the CSP meta is PREPENDED to head, href and xlink:href are forbidden, and the result is re-parsed so a parser-mutation payload cannot reintroduce a link.

The fixed bootstrap that runs inside the opaque iframe: the bundle is base64 into a script literal so a </script> in the HTML cannot break out, and the asset Blob URLs are created INSIDE the frame because an opaque origin cannot load a parent-created URL.
Fatal UTF-8 decoding (invalid sequences throw rather than becoming U+FFFD) and a chunked base64 encoder, the chunking existing because String.fromCharCode blows the argument limit on a large payload.
The borderless full-size iframe and the status line; the only floor on the preview height is min-height 240px.

Two modes: static (srcDoc, sandbox='') and scripted (a Blob iframe with sandbox=allow-scripts and NO allow-same-origin); the frame is keyed by its Blob URL so a replaced document cannot keep running, and the URL is revoked on replace and unmount.

The HTML registration and its injected face: the interactive mode is gated on the developer-tools preference, and the related-file read uses the session from the ADDRESS with baseFile so the Host resolves the relative path and controls read authority.
The documentHtml dictionary; 'frame' is the iframe's accessible name so a screen reader announces what the frame contains.

The finite dependency packer: only direct classic .js and stylesheet .css references, 4 MiB per asset / 32 MiB total / 64 assets, a base element leaves resolution to the browser, and exceeding any limit rejects the whole package rather than publishing a partial one.

Adapts the relative read: one decode, query/fragment stripped, absolute and non-relative forms refused, and the OBSERVED dependency is the Host-resolved absolute path (or the Host's own error.details.path) — never a guessed one.
The image frame follows the scroller's width so the image's percentage maximum resolves against the pane and never scrolls horizontally; margin auto centres it shrunk or not.

Renders the bytes as a Blob URL in an img; the URL is revoked on replace/unmount, the image is only revealed after onLoad, a Blob failure and a decode failure both give the localized message, and a zoom change keeps the same img and the same URL so an animated image keeps playing.
The image registration with its own zoom store and tab-lifetime retention; SVG is deliberately EXCLUDED from the binary list so its XML source stays readable and keeps the plain-text fallback.
The sidebarImage dictionary, spread from the shared zoom copy so it is self-contained; 'preview' is the image's alt text and therefore its accessible name.

The browser half: provides the DocumentPreviewRegistry via reflect, registers the type/dictionaries/body/title, declares four child slots, and calls the eight renderer registrations; every import from another plugin is type-only.
Centred loading column and its compact inline variant (width/height 100% with min-height 0 so it centres in the body's content box).
One shared loading affordance: a 28px StateDot centred, or 14px inline that keeps the accessible label but drops the visible text.
The sidebarDocumentPreview dictionary; zh is the key source and en is typed against it, so a missing translation is a compile error.
The key/value grid inside the frontmatter box, with display:contents making each pair one grid row.

Frontmatter field list: strings show their resolved value while every other node shows its AUTHORED source text, recovered from the node range and de-indented; invalid or non-mapping YAML returns undefined for the verbatim fallback.
Splits a leading YAML frontmatter block with one anchored regex that accepts --- or ... as the closing delimiter and an empty block, and treats an unterminated block as Markdown.
Registers the Markdown implementation for md/markdown at the builtin band with wrap false — the document does not consume the wrap preference.
The documentMarkdown dictionary, carrying the shared primitive's own labels (code copy, footnotes) because the primitive is untranslated.
The Markdown container (prose whitespace inside the source-oriented body) and the frontmatter metadata box, which is empty-collapsed and never heading text.

One retained Markdown renderer over the accumulated text, with the YAML parser lazily loaded only when frontmatter exists and the VERBATIM block as both the Suspense fallback and the chunk-rejection fallback.
Turns a Markdown image destination into a file-route URL: one decode, query/fragment stripped from the file name, Windows drive letters accepted, every other scheme refused.

The Office PDF cache: identity is (renderer generation, session, absolute path, source version), every read re-authorises before reuse, one reader cancelling does not cancel the shared conversion (refcounted), background reads get one slot less, and LRU eviction honours both entry and byte limits.
Binds the conversion read to the store actions and to the owner's loaded/failed callbacks, so the store and the owner can never disagree; an aborted signal does nothing at all.
The warning button and the fixed, portal-positioned font panel, sized with min()/calc() so it can be taller than its anchor.

The anchored non-modal missing-fonts panel: portaled to document.body, positioned only once known (visibility hidden until then), focus moved in and returned, Escape and outside-click close it, and nothing is retained between mounts.

The Office registration: it survives a missing Host renderer (the read rejects with localized guidance), the authorisation probe is a 1-byte read plus a stat, conversion reasons are mapped to locale keys, and connection/reset replaces the whole cache.
The Office dictionary with nine distinct failure messages, each naming a different next step, plus the missing-font copy and the enable-the-service guidance.
An 86-byte flex column so the nested PDF scrollport gets a definite height.
Loads one Office revision and delegates rendering to a NESTED keyed PDF slot; the load effect does not depend on the load callback's identity, so a new callback alone does not restart the conversion.
The toolbar's missing-font warning, rendered only for the revision currently displayed so a stale font list cannot be shown next to a new document.
Retains the converted Office preview across body remounts; every write is stamped with the content revision, and a failure drops the previous file so a stale PDF is never shown beside a fresh error.
Hand-written ambient declaration for the pdfjs-dist worker ?raw import, standing in for the custom bundler resolver that actually satisfies it.

The BinaryDataFactory that serves PDF.js cmaps, standard fonts and wasm from build-inlined base64 with no network fallback; every request returns a fresh transferable buffer and an unbundled filename throws.

Page rendering with cancellation: the raster allocation is capped at 16,777,216 PIXELS by lowering the ratio while the CSS display size stays the viewport's, and page.cleanup() runs only after the render settles.
One structured error class for Worker failures, distinct from a parse error, with the native Event kept only as a cause.
Registers the PDF renderer (binary, bytes-complete, no wrap) and exposes pdfBodyRegistration, which the Office preview reuses through a nested keyed slot instead of duplicating the PDF code.
Loads the PDF chunk only when a PDF body mounts, keeping PDF.js, the worker source and the embedded cmaps out of the startup bundle.
The PDF dictionary spread from the shared zoom copy, with distinct keys for a password-protected file and a dead Worker.

The PDF reader: pages render lazily via IntersectionObserver, renders are serialised through a promise chain because PDF.js shares a page proxy, the previous bitmap stays visible until the replacement is ready, and the text layer is PDF.js's official TextLayerBuilder.
The page sequence and a faithful port of pdfjs-dist's text-layer CSS (rotation transforms, scale factors, selection colour) so the overlay aligns exactly with the canvas.

Opens a PDF with an explicitly owned version-matched Worker: the source is inlined and a ready marker appended, the app waits for that acknowledgement before getDocument, there is deliberately NO main-thread fallback, and disposal awaits document.destroy() before terminating the Worker.
Restorable PDF viewing preferences (last visible page, optional zoom) keyed by tab; the document objects and canvases stay component-local.

The selectable text overlay built with PDF.js's official TextLayerBuilder, so selection boundaries and copy normalisation are the library's; scale composes viewport.scale with userUnit and cancel() releases the shared selection listener.
The address-to-read translation: hostFileOf takes the session from the address alone and throws for a non-session address, and the page length is deliberately not sent so the Host's own cap applies.

The preview's state: pages keyed by their first line, the view (scroll, wrap, answered revision) preserved across a reset, the observedVersion baseline that stops a change during a read being announced as a change, and a page of a newer version dropping the older pages.
The plain-text fallback: it declares NO extensions (it is offered by the owner, not by suffix matching) and is priority builtin so a dedicated implementation always outranks it.

The page arithmetic: linesOf distinguishes a page holding one empty line from a page past EOF, and scrollToLine handles both the plain row and the code block's pre .line, returning false when the renderer exposes no such line.
One pre per page and one div per line, with the line identity derived from the page offset so the navigation target is the file's line number, not the page's.
The body's layout, hand-matched to the conversation header's 38px rule position, with :has() selectors that hand the scroller over to the code and PDF renderers.

The body: selects a renderer from the registry, issues loadPage/loadAll/prepareRenderer, renders the chosen implementation through the keyed slot, and renders the unsupported state WITHOUT issuing a read for a known-binary suffix.
Reads the tab title from the tab info hook and renders the file-type icon before it.
The shared zoom copy, exported as two spreadable fragments rather than a registered namespace, so there is exactly one copy of the six strings.
Tab-local zoom preferences in a per-session store factory, with the tab-lifetime channel (retainTab) the only way the state is forgotten.
The zoom vocabulary: a discriminated union (fit-width | fixed scale) because fit must keep tracking the pane while a fixed 100% must not, plus the bounds and the menu presets as separate constants.
The floating control's reveal animation, forced visible on devices without hover, with reduced-motion support and tabular numerals so the percentage does not jitter mid-gesture.
The zoom toolbar: an imperative showZoom handle updates the percentage during a pinch without re-rendering the document tree, and the stepper rounds to the step grid instead of multiplying.
The frame, scrollport and reveal zone, with the two surface sizing modes expressed purely in CSS from the --document-zoom and --document-zoom-width variables.

Fit-width never upscales, the Ctrl+wheel gesture is pointer-anchored (the point under the cursor stays put) and commits to a fixed scale only after a 120 ms settle, and the tab signal cancels a pending gesture.
The schemastery schema for the Office cache and Excel parser limits; every field is min(1) so a zero is REJECTED rather than read as unlimited, and the client re-validates the host's injected config.
Ambient declaration for *.module.css giving the class map a Record<string,string> type (so a typo is not a compile error).
The HOST half: validates the config and injects it into every served browser page as the global __DSH_DOCUMENT_PREVIEW_CONFIG__, withdrawing it on disposal.

Asserts the exact ordered list of 12 registered seats with their components, that the seat key is the implementation id rather than the kind, and that no later renderer may steal a suffix the code highlighter owns.
Two parser-mutation payloads (MathML href, mglyph/style) must leave no href after a re-parse, and the CSP meta must be the FIRST element in head with exactly one meta[http-equiv].

Proves the streaming highlighter keeps one CodeBlock and one pre.shiki across page growth, carries a multiline comment's grammar state over a page boundary, and yields the same token stream as the settled document.

Proves the metadata is published BEFORE the document slot exists, that disposal removes metadata/body/dictionary, and that the dedicated HTML and Markdown builtins stay ahead of the shared code highlighter.
Pinpoints the eight default limits and asserts a zero limit THROWS for every key, which is why '0 = unlimited' can never be introduced here by accident.

Proves the unresolved path is preserved byte-for-byte in the content id (../, %252e%252e), that a narrower type at the extension band takes the address while the text type stays a candidate, and the fallback band is ranked by literal pattern length.

Packs the package and asserts the exact require.async chunk list in client.js, that no chunk statically requires another, that the third-party licence texts are present verbatim, and boots the lazy chunks in a node:vm context with React as the only external.
Proves the snapshot identity is stable between changes, that a binary suffix outside extensions throws and leaves the registry empty, and that a duplicate id keeps the original.
Drives the PRODUCTION Sidebar and Slot renderer: the body receives a resource snapshot with no operations and no ctx, and switching the selected implementation does not change the tab.
Proves the same CodeBody element survives pagination, the plain-text option appears for .svg/.html but not for .png/.pdf, and a binary suffix hides the viewer control entirely.
One sample from every category matches, case and separators do not matter, and twelve non-matches — including private.key and a directory named work.md — stay unviewable.

Asserts the FortuneSheet options exactly (allowEdit false, forceCalculation false, showToolbar false, cellContextMenu ['copy']) and that a ResizeObserver dispatches a synthetic window resize; five parse failures each map to their locale key.

Proves a cached formula result of 0 or false survives (ExcelJS's cell.value would lose it), that a formula with no cache renders blank and counts, and that the theme tint maths is numerically correct.
Adds a hand-written chart part, a drawing part, their rels and a conditional-formatting rule to the styled fixture, with or without a DrawingML namespace prefix.
Proves a charted workbook yields EXACTLY the same sheets as the baseline, the source bytes are unchanged, the omission is idempotent, and a comment VML is retained and not reported.
Generates the styled multi-sheet workbook, an HTML-looking-text workbook, a meeting-minutes workbook with 27 uncached formulas, and a freeze-matrix workbook.

Proves the 1904 epoch shift, that CSV values stay literal strings ('00123', '=SUM(1,2)' with no formula property, 'TRUE'), and that damaged/renamed/hidden-only/oversized legacy workbooks are rejected.
Loads the six committed independent-writer OPC workbooks by name; the case list is the regression index (five isolated failures plus one combined).
Runs every OPC case against BOTH the Node and the browser-bundle ExcelJS entries, and reverses the relationship and ZIP entry order to prove comment binding does not depend on either.
Derives the four opening regressions by changing exactly one package property each: Strict URI aliases, root-target case, part-name case, and an orphan DrawingML.
Proves ambiguous ASCII case-equivalent ZIP entries are REJECTED before filtering can hide either, while non-ASCII names (Ä.xml vs ä.xml) stay distinct.
Proves the transferred buffer is a copy, the input survives the transfer, thirteen malformed Worker messages are all rejected, and no Worker is allocated for an aborted or oversized input.
Models a clamping scroll container (jsdom does not clamp) and asserts the workbook context follows the clamped offsets, including a reversed gesture after the leading edge.
Proves the Excel registration never touches the Office service, that csv/tsv are not binary, and that the injected value is exactly { limits }.
Proves the Worker protocol: parsed sheets on success, 'invalid' for a parser crash, 'tooLarge' at maxCells 1, and no 'unknown' category.
Loads the eight committed encoding-equivalent workbooks by name.

Proves UTF-16 with and without a BOM yields a preview identical to the UTF-8 baseline, the retained parts are byte-identical to the source, a missing core part fails, and a vbaProject.bin is not decoded as XML.

Settles every stale/current combination in both orders for success and failure across page, byte and mode-switch paths, and proves the read runs under the ADDRESS's session rather than the injected one.
One sentence per code, the byte limit rendered in B/KB/MB, and the recourse mapping: not-text and too-large offer 'open', not-found and not-regular-file offer 'none', everything else retries.
The shared body harness: a real store, a real face over a scripted read, a scripted useResource, and a settle() that ticks twice because the face registers its store write synchronously.

Binary OOXML package (8,781 bytes, ZIP magic 50 4B 03 04, 17 entries incl. xl/charts/chart1.xml and xl/comments/comment1.xml); not read line by line because it is a compressed binary archive — its purpose is established by tests/excel-opc.client.spec.ts and the fuzz README.
Binary OOXML package (6,261 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the isolated Openpyxl comments case — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by tests/excel-opc-fixture.ts.
Binary OOXML package (4,898 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the isolated part-name case — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the OPC spec.
Binary OOXML package (4,907 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the isolated namespace-prefix case — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the OPC spec.

Binary OOXML package (5,325 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the isolated relative-relationship-target case from XlsxWriter 3.2.9 — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the OPC spec.
Binary OOXML package (5,575 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the isolated Table case — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the OPC spec.
Binary OOXML package (11,224 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the CDATA-text variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by tests/excel-xml.client.spec.ts.
Binary OOXML package (11,332 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the relocated-parts variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the XML spec.

Binary OOXML package (11,184 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed; 21 entries incl. xl/media/image1.png and xl/drawings/vmlDrawing1.vml); the baseline workbook every other variant is compared against — not read line by line (binary ZIP).
Binary OOXML package (11,183 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the relocated sharedStrings.xml variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the XML spec.
Binary OOXML package (11,196 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the relocated styles.xml variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the XML spec.
Binary OOXML package (11,456 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the UTF-16 metadata encoding variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the XML spec.
Binary OOXML package (11,552 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the UTF-16 worksheet encoding variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the XML spec.
Binary OOXML package (11,172 bytes, ZIP magic confirmed); the relocated workbook.xml variant — not read line by line (binary ZIP), purpose established by the XML spec.

A 81-byte YAML configuration override (office.maxCachedEntries 2) for an Office-cache scenario — not read line by line because it is a two-line config fragment read as part of the cache scenario, not a source module.
The fuzz Worker's isolation: it reports the input-unchanged check from inside the Worker and collects up to eight cause-chain levels so a failure report says WHY.

The corpus generator: the oracle is re-read with Openpyxl so the parser is never compared against itself, ZIP metadata is fixed for byte reproducibility, and eight structural mutations change the encoding without changing the cell semantics.
Per-heading bilingual hash record for the fuzz manual.

The campaign manual: the generate/run/replay loop, the retained-regression catalogue, the report semantics, and the honest statement that accepted-corrupt inputs are informational and the repros are not globally minimal.
Chinese translation of the campaign manual, preserving the same caveats in the same places.

The campaign runner: a terminatable Worker with a 10 s deadline and a 256 MB heap cap per input, bytes transferred, and a six-way outcome taxonomy (pass / rejected-valid / accepted-corrupt / value-mismatch / notice-mismatch / mutated-source).
Proves the related-file read uses the session FROM THE ADDRESS with baseFile set to the addressed document, and that an absolute address throws.

Drives the whole preview so a .css/.js dependency change re-reads root and dependency and replaces the frame, and proves the static mode releases the dependency subscriptions while the root stays watched.

Executes the in-frame bootstrap in a node:vm context and asserts exactly one </script> in the output, the non-ASCII text absent from the outer HTML, the script order and defer/async attributes preserved, and invalid UTF-8 rejected.
Enumerates eleven unsupported dependency forms that must cause NO read at all, and exercises the total-byte, per-asset-byte and asset-count limits separately.
Proves the observed dependency is the HOST-RESOLVED absolute path, never the authored spelling, and that no path is guessed when a failure carries none.
Proves the Blob URL is revoked on replace and unmount and that a zoom change does NOT recreate the image or the Blob, so an animated image keeps playing.
Proves the title function is not called at registration, and that retainTab twice with one signal still forgets the tab exactly once.
Pinpoints the page arithmetic: a trailing newline produces a final empty line matching the Host's count, and lines 0 and lines 1 are different things.
The loading affordance: 28px centred with visible text, 14px inline with the label only in aria-label.

Proves the same heading element and the same pre.shiki survive page growth and settlement, that reference definitions and KaTeX only resolve at EOF, and the ten-key frontmatter field list including folded scalars, lists and aliases.
A chunk that throws on import must leave the verbatim frontmatter and the body heading intact.
Proves the deployment prefix survives, the hash is dropped, fourteen unsupported destinations are refused, and the Desktop scheme dsh-app:// works.
Proves the Markdown body renders without calling useTabInfo at all and that the locale function identity survives a language switch.

Proves the whole sharing contract: a cancelled reader leaves the conversion running, a late-cancelled conversion is discarded, a changed source is not retained, a matching version with a different canonical source is not reused, and the borrowed buffer is reused without copying.
Proves focus moves into the panel and back to the trigger, a blur into the panel's own button does not close it, and nothing is retained between mounts.

Proves the registration survives a missing Host renderer, the authorisation probe is a 1-byte read, a source replaced between probe and stat refuses the cached bytes, and ten conversion reasons map to their locale keys.
Proves the factory never falls back to the network, refuses a prototype key ('toString'), and returns a buffer that survives PDF.js transferring it away.

Proves the previous bitmap stays visible while a new zoom render is in flight, a Ctrl+wheel gesture updates the display but does not write the store until it settles, and only nearby pages are rendered and re-rendered.

Drives cancellation with controlled promises: cleanup runs only after the render settles, a getPage settling after cancellation never touches the canvas, and the raster cap is hit exactly at 16,777,216 pixels.
Hand-written deterministic PDFs with an explicit xref table — a two-page colour fixture and a journal-like selection fixture — so the bytes are stable and clock-free.
Proves the lazy body's fallback is the shared loading indicator, retainTab twice with one signal forgets once, and the registered body is LazyPdfBody (the chunk boundary is part of the contract).

Proves the module-worker options exactly, that getDocument is not called before the handshake, that the bytes handed over are a copy, and that disposal awaits document.destroy() before terminating the Worker.
Runs the REAL PDF.js in a Node worker thread and asserts the centre pixel colour of each of the two pages — the only test in the shard exercising a third-party library end to end.
Proves the per-tab page/zoom retention, the one-tab forget, and that two store INSTANCES are independent even for the same tab id.
Proves the overlay's scale is recomputed on resize (0.5 to 0.25) and that cancel() disconnects the observer, cancels the layer and removes the DOM.
A 749-byte port of the browser worker API over Node's parentPort, which is what makes the real-library smoke test possible.

Proves a superseded load's late loaded('v1') cannot move the version after v2 landed, that a failure retries only after another file change, and that replace/close/hide each abort the pending conversion.
Proves the first metadata frame is a baseline, a repeated identical failure is not a change but a recovery is, and adding the same address twice subscribes once.
Proves the address's path is decoded exactly once and the absolute path is preserved verbatim, and that six non-session address shapes throw.
Proves the page table, the version drop, the failure-beside-pages rule, that reset keeps the view, and the observedVersion baseline retained across overlapping reads.

Supplies jsdom's missing geometry (offsetTop = line number times line height) and pins the remount-reads-nothing rule, the scroll-to-end-loads-the-next-page rule and the navigation-answered-once rule.
Proves the chip icon is 16px and aria-hidden and that the Markdown and PDF sheets differ.
A real BIFF8 compound-file fixture with a hand-written CellParsedFormula token stream, a hidden sheet, a merge and the 1904 flag.
Proves the fixed and fit-width preferences are stored as values and that forget drops one tab.
Proves fit-width never upscales, a pointer-anchored zoom keeps the surface point under the cursor, the 72 px reveal zone and 420 ms hide delay, and that no timer survives unmount.
The client project's include list and its 20 project references — the package's real dependency graph written out.
The host project compiles ONLY src/index.ts and src/config.ts (files, not include), so browser code cannot be pulled into the host build.
The composite root referencing the host and client projects separately.

The build config with three custom plugins: a PDF.js worker-source resolver, a nested Rolldown build that re-bundles the Excel worker as an IIFE string (so the outer build's licence analysis sees its imports), and the inlined base64 PDF.js assets.
Marketplace metadata: {"meta":{"title":"ui-sidebar-files"}}.
Chinese marketplace metadata: title 文件浏览面板 plus a description that names the right-Sidebar preview.
Manifest for @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-files: no runtime dependencies at all, a peerDependency on cordis, and the dsh.client.inject list.
Bilingual-pair hash record for the files README, with hashes independent of the preview package's.

The file tree's contract: the type claims no address, the root is the session cwd, levels are keyed by absolute path, a file row opens a session-scoped address RELATIVE to the tree root, and the scroll offset is committed once on unmount.
Chinese translation of the same contract, read in full; it keeps the load-bearing sentence about the root-relative address.
The files tab type: no patterns at all (it claims no address), builtin band, one guide entry at order 10 with the GuideArtworkFiles glyph, and a title function evaluated per locale.

One open directory's ownership: the watch loop, the dirty-flag read coalescer, watch-unsupported treated as a degraded mode rather than a failure, and a child that disappears having its whole subtree collapsed.

The tree's async half: the Remote stream supervisor with an ended handler, a per-tab per-path generation counter so the latest listing wins, and childPath joining with / whatever the parent's separators are.
The tree's layout, including the 2 px scrollbar inset and stable gutter reproduced from the workspace list, and rows that abut with the air coming from the inset.

The tree's body: directories first then a natural case-insensitive name order, a non-clickable greyed row for 'other' entries, and the scroll offset written ONCE on unmount so scrolling never re-renders the tree.
The chip title: a 16px folder FileTypeIcon before the type's label; the tree's own rows never draw it.

The browser half: the workspace.files shortcut with per-platform defaults (Linux Web left unbound) and a resolve that can return a localized 'blocked' reason, plus the type, dictionary, body and title registrations.
The sidebarFiles dictionary, with the namespace declaration kept next to the key set so any module naming the namespace needs only this file.
The tree's view state: levels keyed by absolute path, and loaded() pruning a directory that was removed or became a file (its expansion entries and whole subtree of levels are dropped).
Ambient CSS-module declarations, byte-identical to the sibling package's copy.
An intentionally empty host half so the package can be mounted on the Host without contributing anything.

Proves the shortcut's blocked path returns the localized reason when there is no session, the handled path opens the tab for the command target, and disposal removes the command, type, seats and dictionary.
Proves the type claims NO address (candidates is empty) and that patterns is undefined, and renders the guide icon at 26px.
Proves two change events during one list produce exactly two lists, that manual refresh consumes pending changes without enabling automatic refresh, and that collapsing awaits every watch release.

Proves the root is subscribed BEFORE it is listed and that the listing waits for ready, that the latest listing of a level wins in either settlement order, and that a watch failure is recorded without an 'Error:' prefix.

Drives the real body over a real store and face: the scroll offset is still 0 in the store while the user scrolls, the PathLabel clips with a ResizeObserver, and a refresh failure appears beside the existing rows without clearing them.
Proves the folder icon is 16px and aria-hidden before the type's label; the manifest records this path with the .tsx extension and the file on disk is .tsx (it contains JSX).
The body harness: a real store and a real face over the scripted list/watch, and a remount() that simulates a tab switch over the same store.
The deferred directory reader, distinguishing the oldest pending call from the newest so the latest-wins rule can be tested in both orders.
The scripted watch streams: a two-phase delivery handshake and a holdRelease() gate that lets a spec assert the close is still pending.

Proves the pruning rule in two shapes (removed and became-a-file) with the sibling's cache surviving, that reset keeps expansion, scroll and auto-refresh, and that writing a level for an unstarted tab THROWS.
Proves the stream is named, the ended handler is invoked once with the readiness flag, an already-cancelled node creates NO stream, and a frame delivered after cancellation is not yielded.
A single client project (unlike the preview package's two) with 13 references.
A 3-line build config with no custom plugins — the contrast with the preview package's 120-line one is the whole difference between the two packages.
